title: CR functions at CR singularities approximation, extension, and hulls

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The definition is announced with 'We say:' but no definitions of the extension, approximation, fixed-neighborhood extension, or fixed-neighborhood approximation properties are actually given. The text immediately jumps to 'A standard procedure...'. Later observations about CR_H and CR_P having these properties are therefore undefined.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3, observation about Levi-flat hypersurface Im z_n = 0
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The claim that any M contained in Im z_n = 0 fails the fixed-neighborhood extension property is false. For example, M = {z_n = 1} is contained in Im z_n = 0, and every CR_H function on M is holomorphic in z' and extends to the fixed neighborhood C^{n-1} × {|z_n - 1| < 1}. Also, the proposed functions 1/(z_n - iε) have poles at iε, which do not approach points with z_n(q) ≠ 0, so they do not obstruct a fixed neighborhood at arbitrary q.

X is defined only with z_3 = 1/k for k ∈ ℕ. Since the boundary of an attached analytic disc is connected, z_3 must be constant on the boundary and hence must equal 1/k for some k. The case z_3 = 0 is impossible, yet the example proceeds to analyze hypothetical z_3 = 0 discs as if X had a z_3 = 0 component.

For X_2 the defining condition is Im z_2 < 0. An attached disc in X_2 must have its z_2-coordinate constant and equal to a boundary value in X_2, so the disc hull should have Im z_2 < 0, not Im z_2 ≤ 0. The written inequality includes points with 1 < |z_1| ≤ 2 and z_2 = ±1 that are not reachable by discs attached to X_2.

Since 1 is not in the open unit disk D, D \ {1} is just D. The intended domain is presumably the closed disk punctured at 1, usually written as \overline{D} \ {1}, because the construction needs convergence on the boundary except at the point 1.
